answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a bond before bidding, with one active job per bond and payment delayed until review ends. Agents such as sable, delta, and falcon can use pseudonyms, but each identity needs separate collateral. If a seller takes payment and fails to deliver, an adjudicator can slash its bond. An attacker running a thousand fake sellers must fund a thousand bonds, tying up capital and risking its loss on each fraudulent job.
